game_identity.player_fantasy: Be the last maintenance runner carrying unstable charge from a central core to failing relays fast enough to keep the network alive.
game_identity.central_interaction: Route, recharge, carry, and transfer charge between a central core and four decaying relay beacons.

playable_loop: Move -> recharge at core -> choose upper/lower passage -> carry charge -> read changing relay urgency -> choose which relay to service -> touch beacon to transfer -> manage decay -> stabilize all four or black out -> retry

controls.move: WASD, arrow keys, or standard-mapped gamepad left stick / D-pad
controls.restart: R, Restart button, or standard-mapped gamepad Start

technology_stack: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript Canvas; local/offline browser; no dependencies
current_milestone: Decision Chain Slice: prove that one service decision materially changes the next meaningful service decision so the existing route/urgency loop behaves like an evolving maintenance chain rather than isolated snapshots or a static target order. Start from one normal-run state with at least two plausible non-dominated relay choices, execute both under the same bounded continuation policy through the next meaningful service decision, and measure how the first choice changes runner position/charge, relay energies, route cost, online/offline exposure, recovery burden, or plausible next targets. Both branches must remain non-terminal long enough to expose that next decision. Test the accepted geometry/decay/readability model before adding hazards, relay classes, resources, scoring, another chamber, or a new primary verb. Human/fresh-player PLAYTESTED evidence remains required before claims that the decision chain is perceived, understandable, fair, tense, balanced, or fun.
known_failures: Accepted main still has no full normal-input WON session reported PLAYTESTED by a genuine human/fresh player; this remains a validation gap, not an autonomous progression gate.
Accepted main still has no full normal-input BLACKOUT session reported PLAYTESTED by a genuine human/fresh player; this remains a validation gap, not an autonomous progression gate.

Accepted main exposes live relay percentages and contextual state/transfer cues, but no genuine fresh-player evidence shows that a human interprets relay urgency, route-versus-urgency tradeoffs, or chained service decisions correctly.

Literal packaged file:// or localhost launch remains blocked in some specialist environments despite structural wiring tests; accepted route/readability inspection used exact repository runtime/presentation bytes in real Chromium with inlining only to bypass that navigation restriction.
Standard-mapped gamepad behavior is covered by simulated Gamepad API regression evidence, but physical gamepad hardware and cross-browser Gamepad API behavior remain unverified.
build_run_instructions: Open index.html in a modern desktop browser, or run python -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000.

evidence_status.tradeoff_slice: COMPLETED on accepted main. World PR #35 is merged as test-only evidence against the unchanged accepted runtime. A naturally reached 13.30s upper-passage snapshot has runner charge 96.45% and relay energies R1 53.38 / R2 49.69 / R3 0.00 / R4 0.00. From that exact state, nearby safer R1 takes about 0.87s to reach while urgent offline R3 takes about 2.04s; equal 1.00s service leaves 44.83% runner charge and 2 relays online for R1 versus 39.22% and 3 relays online for R3. Independent Systems reproduction confirmed the measurements and quantified lower immediate network recovery burden on the urgent branch. The Game Director accepts this as sufficient autonomous evidence that route cost and live urgency compete without a new mechanic.
evidence_status.decision_chain_slice: OPEN / NOT YET PROVEN. Accepted evidence currently branches one coupled decision only through an immediate controlled service horizon. The next evidence target is to continue both plausible branches under the same bounded policy until each exposes a next meaningful service decision, then measure how the first choice changes that next decision state. No new runtime mechanic is justified until the existing model is tested for this chain.
